text.tspan: Part 2 – Multi-agent Collusion Simulation: Logical Architecture
Badges = brief points 1–10 · orchestrator, builder, checks and gate are deterministic code · agents never talk directly · outputs are simulated risk patterns, never findings of fact
• Scenario knowledge: what records each role
• Profile content enters cards as ASSUMPTION
• Discovery: S1…S5 singly and in pairs + params
• Recall (eval only): MO and MO-combo scenarios
• Negative controls: S5, S1, S2 → expect NO_SCHEME
• Limits: 4 rounds · ≤3 msgs per actor per turn
· 10 min per run · simulated tokens · rng_seed
• SHA-256 of raw AND normalised text
• Source text kept in data fields, apart from
prevent it (LLMs have no hard boundary)
• Heuristic flags → trace; flagged spans never
• Annex B text → scenario builder (as data)
• Annex A + annotations → Review Agent only
SIMULATION SANDBOX – agents have no network, file or tool access except through the orchestrator
only if review or gate asks;
Final run states (every run ends in exactly one) · CONVERGED or SOLO commits enter the pipeline
Commit rule: proposer counts as accepting; every actor with a step must accept or hold a can_be_unwitting step; solo = proposer's steps only.
Non-card states → run report: metadata only (state, counts, reason codes, trace_ref), checked by the gate.
• Private: own reasoning and draft offers
• Doesn't know: records the provider files
• Actions: enrol · attend / sign · submit claim
• Channels: public · private with Provider, Employer
out-of-role action · forbidden tool · injected-text echo
• Private: own reasoning and draft offers
• Channels: public · private with Trainee, Employer
out-of-role action · forbidden tool · injected-text echo
• Private: own reasoning and draft offers
• Actions: hire / release · sponsor fee · confirm
• Channels: public · private with Trainee, Provider
out-of-role action · forbidden tool · injected-text echo
* Recruiters (S3, MO-04) and sponsors (MO-08) are modelled as Provider / Employer capabilities – a stated limitation.
• Each action in its actor's library
unwitting = has a step, no accept
• For each of the 7 actor subsets:
can it reach the objective by
ANY path, not just this one?
• Rules (code): schema + origin labels, banned-term lists, named-entity check, specificity heuristics
• Classifier (production; mocked in PoC): “more concrete than Annex A” and evasion detail – rules alone are easy to evade
• Runs twice: rule pre-check before the Review Agent, full gate after; also checks every run report
• Stamps every card “SIMULATED – NOT A FINDING OF FACT”
• Blocked → one revision (shared budget), else REJECTED_IN_PIPELINE
codes + field pointers only – no MO text or IDs, ≤1 revision
Agents never write files. Writers: orchestrator (traces), approval service (decisions), eval harness (reports). PoC isolation = in-process; production = separate containers.
SIMULATED – NOT A FINDING OF FACT
• steps[]: actor, action, preconditions, effects, origin
• flows[]: from → to, type, visibility, origin
• status: set only by approval service
Novelty rules (7) – use our MO annotations (actor set, core mechanisms), labelled ASSUMPTION:
known = same actor set and core mechanisms · variation = shares a core mechanism, differs in actors or steps · new = no core match
new: no evidence threshold – flagged 'emerging, low evidence' and needs two reviewers. source_support: 0 none · 1 unverified excerpt only
· 2 matches an observed MO mechanism · 3 several observed MOs. Recall runs (MO scenarios) are excluded from novelty claims.
Plausibility = realism checks (code, pass / fail); there is no separate LLM plausibility score.
detects edits; no key, so not a signature
• Back-test the pattern on historical claims
• Fairness review: does the rule target groups
• Append-only JSONL per run; runs written one at a time (file lock) into a hash-chained runs manifest
• Head hash kept outside the repo and printed in each run summary (production: write-once object storage)
• Events: sanitiser flags, every message, tool call with args (allowed / denied), validation, retry, abstention,
final state, review output, gate results, human decision with rationale and card hash
• Spans: per-agent latency and simulated tokens · replay = recorded responses (not rng_seed)
• Restricted access · repo ships gate-checked, redacted sample traces from synthetic mock runs (stated in README)
Needs a real model (mocks prove nothing)
Mock runs – must be exact: schema-valid 100% · origin labels match oracle · planner results match oracle · every adversarial script blocked
Real model – n ≥ 20 per scenario: false-scheme rate on negatives · citation support vs hand-labelled set (counts, small n) · cost and latency
test fixtures (incl. injected annex text) enter through the sanitiser – end-to-end
Production path (designed, not built in the PoC)
• Mock adapter → approved model endpoint behind an internal model gateway with per-agent scopes and cost limits (the MCP gateway from Part 1)
• Agents in separate containers · trace store on access-controlled, write-once storage · human review in a web UI with SSO
= brief point: 1 profiles · 2 messages · 3 boundaries · 4 patterns · 5 actor removal · 6 source separation ·
7 MO classification · 8 schemas / limits · 9 safeguards / approval · 10 traces / evals
Arrows point from sender to receiver. Dashed boxes = future or outside the PoC.
